notes:
Summary: mid-market product company building an in-app conversational assistant + developer code-assist features. Initially evaluating Redwood Hosted API for fast time-to-value; after hosted demo they requested a Dedicated POC to validate consistent latency and unit economics at scale. High-level goals: keep p95 latency for chat < 150ms for common queries, sustain 40-60 req/s for peak flows, and reduce per-1k-token inference cost vs current managed endpoints by 20-35%.

Key technical preferences/asks:
- Models: leaning toward an open-weights family (LlamaX-13B variant) with fallback to smaller quantized variants for low-cost paths. Asked about Redwood model catalog and verified latency profiles.
- Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to cheaper quantized model when Dedicated pool saturated; need canary rollouts for model upgrades.
- Caching: interested in prefix/KV caching on LLM responses for repeated prompts (product FAQs). Wants cache TTL controls and hit-rate metrics in Console.
- Batching & throughput: workshop showed they can tolerate micro-batching up to 20 tokens/window for background embeddings, but chat needs tight latency budget; asked for guidance on continuous batching thresholds and CPU/GPU tradeoffs.
- Quantization profiles: asked for recommended 4-bit and 8-bit profiles, impact on quality (ROUGE/semantic similarity), and fallbacks. SE Daniel proposed two quant profiles: q4f high-quality (slower) and q4b cost-optimized (faster).
- Unit economics: ran sensitivity with Redwood Optimize suggestions — estimated hosted API cost baseline $0.40/1k tokens; Dedicated with batching + q4b profile projected $0.10-$0.18/1k tokens depending on average sequence length and cache hit-rate.

POC scope & success metrics:
- 2-week Dedicated POC in us-west with 2 reserved GPU nodes, run their chat traffic replay for 48 hours and measure p50/p95 latency, token/req cost, and cache hit-rate.
- Acceptance: p95 < 220ms during simulated 70% load, token unit-cost <= $0.20 with >=30% cache hit rate on FAQs, no SSO blockers in deployment.

Commercial & procurement notes:
- Procurement cycle estimated 6-8 weeks. Primary blocker: internal security wants ISO27001 evidence and a KMS integration whitepaper. Finance is price-sensitive; prefer 12-month committed capacity if cost targets met.

- AE to provide committed reserved pricing scenarios and draft contract term-sheet (Priya) - due 2026-02-24.
